selected_evidence.summary: The native persistent daily logrotate timer is enabled and active; the installed rule parses as a one-day rotation policy and remained active after restart.
The installed rule specifies seven rotations and compression; forced rotation produced a valid gzip archive, and the preserved production content passed gzip validation.

selected_evidence.requirement: Application can continue writing after rotation
selected_evidence.summary: A writer held inode 290759 before and after copy-truncate rotation, remained alive, and continued writing successfully through sequence 30.

selected_evidence.requirement: Preserve existing data and clean up validation artifacts
selected_evidence.summary: The decompressed archive matches the original SHA-256 exactly; synthetic markers, temporary files, and test writers were absent in the final state.

selected_evidence.requirement: Keep installed OS, kernel, and compatible software
selected_evidence.summary: RHEL 10.0, kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0, and packaged logrotate 3.22.0 remained installed and unchanged.

Healthy baseline boot ID 050a5b4c-6c7b-42ad-957a-b6a41a0d34db was captured, reboot acknowledgement returned before disconnect, and the recovered node reported changed boot ID 3d160e91-9894-4f11-9510-50ad8f18d87c. Logrotate scheduling, SSH, firewalld, SELinux enforcement, configuration checksum, archive integrity, and preserved data all recovered with zero failed units.
SELinux remained enforcing, firewalld and SSH remained active, listeners were unchanged, no failed units existed, and only the intended rotation rule references the application log.
